statute_title: Driving Under the Influence of Intoxicating Liquor or Drugs
offense_class: Misdemeanor (first through third); Fourth degree Felony (fourth+); Third degree Felony (sixth+)
penalty_max: 90 days (first); 364 days (second); 364 days (third); 18 months (fourth/fifth); 3 years (sixth+); 6 years (eighth+)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within this state
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or any drug
Or had a BAC of 0.08 or more
To a degree that rendered the defendant incapable of safely driving
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours (first); 96 consecutive hours (second); 30 days (third); 6 months (fourth/fifth); 18 months (sixth/seventh); 36 months (eighth+)
notes: New Mexico uses a lifetime lookback for prior DWI convictions. Aggravated DWI (BAC ≥.16 or refusal with impairment) doubles minimum jail time. Ignition interlock required for all convicted offenders. License revocation 1 year (first) to lifetime (eighth+).

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within New Mexico
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC 0.08 or higher, or impaired driving ability
No prior DWI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 24 hours in jail or community service; completion of DWI school; 1-year license revocation
enhancements: Refusal with other evidence of impairment (aggravated)
notes: Mandatory ignition interlock for 1 year. DWI school and community service required. Aggravated first offense doubles jail minimum to 48 hours.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (second/third); Fourth degree Felony (fourth/fifth); Third degree Felony (sixth/seventh); Second degree Felony (eighth+)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within New Mexico
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs
BAC 0.08 or higher, or impaired driving ability
One or more prior DWI convictions (lifetime lookback)
mandatory_minimum: 96 consecutive hours (second); 30 days (third); 6 months (fourth); 18 months (sixth); 36 months (eighth+)
enhancements: Refusal of chemical test with other impairment evidence
Causing great bodily harm or death
notes: New Mexico's lifetime lookback means all prior DWI convictions count regardless of when they occurred. Second offense: 2-year license revocation. Third: 3-year revocation. Fourth+: lifetime revocation (may petition after 5 years). Ignition interlock required for all.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle within New Mexico
While under the influence of any drug to a degree that rendered the defendant incapable of safely driving
Or under the combined influence of intoxicating liquor and any drug
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DWI by offense count
enhancements: Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: No per se drug limits in New Mexico. Prosecution must prove actual impairment. Cannabis remains treated the same as other drugs for DWI purposes despite legalization. Drug Recognition Expert evaluations used.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle
Carelessly and heedlessly in willful or wanton disregard of the rights or safety of others
And without due caution and circumspection
notes: Common plea-down from DWI. Points on driving record. Second offense within one year carries enhanced penalties.

statute_title: Duty Upon Striking Unattended Vehicle or Property / Leaving the Scene
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (great bodily harm or death under § 66-7-201.1); Misdemeanor (injury under § 66-7-201; property damage under § 66-7-203)
penalty_max: 18 months (felony — great bodily harm/death); 1 year (injury); 6 months (property damage)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide required information or render aid
notes: Leaving the scene involving great bodily harm or death is a fourth degree felony. Injury without great bodily harm is a misdemeanor. Property damage only requires stopping and exchanging information.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (DWI involved); Fourth degree Felony (reckless driving); Misdemeanor (negligence)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
While under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs, or in a reckless manner, or with negligence
Proximately causing the death of a human being
notes: New Mexico has a specific vehicular homicide statute with three tiers based on culpability: DWI (most severe), reckless, and negligent. DWI-related vehicular homicide is a third degree felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
With criminal negligence
Proximately causing the death of another person
Not involving DWI or reckless driving
notes: Least severe form of vehicular homicide. Requires criminal negligence — more than ordinary negligence but less than recklessness.

statute_title: Driving While License Suspended or Revoked
offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a highway
While defendant's license was suspended, revoked, or canceled
Defendant had knowledge of the suspension or revocation
notes: Mandatory 7 consecutive days if the suspension was DWI-related. Additional suspension period added to existing revocation.

statute_title: Aggravated Fleeing a Law Enforcement Officer
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: A law enforcement officer attempted to make a lawful stop
Defendant willfully and intentionally fled in a vehicle
In a manner that endangered the life of another person
enhancements: Great bodily harm or death resulting (third degree felony)
notes: Basic eluding (without endangerment) is a misdemeanor under § 66-8-126. Aggravated fleeing (with endangerment) is a fourth degree felony. Great bodily harm or death elevates to third degree felony.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (small amounts most substances); Fourth degree Felony (larger amounts or certain substances)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed on New Mexico controlled substance schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
notes: New Mexico decriminalized small amounts of most drug possession. Cannabis was legalized for adults 21+ in 2021. Drug court diversion widely available.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (>2 oz personal use); Felony (large amounts with intent)
elements: Defendant possessed cannabis
In excess of the amounts permitted under the Cannabis Regulation Act
Legal limit: 2 ounces of flower, 16 grams of extract, 800 mg edibles for adults 21+
notes: New Mexico legalized recreational cannabis for adults 21+ in 2021 (Cannabis Regulation Act). Adults may possess up to 2 oz flower. Exceeding legal limits remains criminal. Under-21 possession is still illegal.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance in New Mexico
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Cocaine possession is a fourth degree felony. No minimum quantity for prosecution. Larger quantities may support trafficking charges.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Methamphetamine possession is a fourth degree felony. Treatment-based diversion and drug courts widely available in New Mexico.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (basic); Second degree Felony (to minors or near schools); First degree Felony (large operations)
penalty_max: 6 years (third degree); 9 years (second degree); 18 years (first degree)
elements: Defendant manufactured, distributed, or possessed with intent to distribute a controlled substance
The substance was a controlled substance under New Mexico law
Defendant acted intentionally
enhancements: Distribution to a minor (one degree higher)
notes: New Mexico trafficking charges are graded by degree. Distribution to minors or near schools elevates by one felony degree. Cannabis trafficking provisions modified by legalization but commercial-scale unlicensed distribution remains criminal.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (most substances); Second degree Felony (to minors/near schools)
elements: Defendant distributed, delivered, or administered a controlled substance
To another person
Knowingly or intentionally
enhancements: Distribution within 1,000 feet of a school
notes: Distribution includes any transfer of controlled substances. Separate provisions for cannabis under the Cannabis Regulation Act for licensed activities.

offense_class: Second degree Felony (Schedule I/II); Third degree Felony (Schedule III-V)
elements: Defendant manufactured, compounded, or produced a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
Knowingly or intentionally
notes: Manufacturing Schedule I or II substances is a second degree felony. Methamphetamine lab cleanup costs may be assessed.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use the paraphernalia to introduce a controlled substance into the body
Paraphernalia as defined in § 30-31-25
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (fourth degree felony)
notes: Possession is a misdemeanor. Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor is a felony. New Mexico has harm reduction provisions that may affect prosecution of syringe possession.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (most substances); Second degree Felony (Schedule I/II to minors/near schools)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With intent to distribute
Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, or other evidence
notes: Intent to distribute is inferred from circumstances. Penalties are the same as for actual distribution.

offense_class: Capital Felony (abolished — life imprisonment)
elements: Defendant willfully, deliberately, and premeditatedly killed another human being
Or killed during the commission of certain felonies (felony murder)
Or by any act greatly dangerous to the lives of others and indicating a depraved mind
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment (30 years minimum before parole eligibility)
enhancements: Felony murder (during kidnapping, sexual assault, robbery, arson, etc.)
notes: New Mexico abolished the death penalty in 2009. Mandatory sentence is life imprisonment with 30-year minimum parole eligibility. Includes three forms: premeditated, felony murder, and depraved-mind murder.

offense_class: Second degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed a killing that would constitute first degree murder
But was done upon a sudden quarrel or in the heat of passion
Or the defendant knew the acts created a strong probability of death or great bodily harm
enhancements: Use of a firearm (§ 31-18-16 — 1 year added)
notes: Second degree murder is a lesser included offense of first degree murder. Covers intentional killings without premeditation and reckless killings with knowledge of extreme danger.

offense_class: Third degree Felony
elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another human being
Upon a sudden quarrel or in the heat of passion
Defendant was sufficiently provoked to kill
enhancements: Use of a firearm (1 year added)
notes: Voluntary manslaughter requires adequate provocation and heat of passion. It is a lesser included offense of second degree murder.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant unlawfully killed another human being
Without the intent to kill
While committing a lawful act in an unlawful manner
Or through criminal negligence
notes: Involuntary manslaughter covers unintentional killings caused by criminal negligence or during the commission of a lawful act done in an unlawful manner.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (with deadly weapon); Third degree Felony (with intent to commit a felony or great bodily harm)
elements: Defendant committed an assault
With a deadly weapon
Or with intent to commit a violent felony on the person assaulted
enhancements: Use of a firearm (§ 31-18-16 — 1 year added)
Against a peace officer, school employee, or healthcare worker
notes: Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon is a fourth degree felony. Aggravated assault with intent to commit a violent felony is a third degree felony.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant attempted to commit a battery upon the person of another
Or used insulting language toward another calculated to provoke a breach of the peace
Or made any threatening gesture or act toward another
notes: New Mexico assault includes attempted battery, threatening gestures, and insulting language. Actual contact constitutes battery, not assault.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally touched or applied force to another person
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
notes: Simple battery is a petty misdemeanor in New Mexico. Aggravated battery (causing great bodily harm) under § 30-3-5 is a third degree felony.

offense_class: Third degree Felony
elements: Defendant, by the use of force or coercion
Took property from the person of another or from the immediate control of another
With intent to deprive the owner permanently
enhancements: Use of a deadly weapon (armed robbery — second degree felony)
notes: Basic robbery without a weapon is a third degree felony. Armed robbery is elevated to second degree felony.

offense_class: Second degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon
notes: Armed robbery is a second degree felony carrying up to 15 years. Firearm enhancement adds 1 year under § 31-18-16.

offense_class: First degree Felony (not voluntarily released); Second degree Felony (voluntarily released unharmed)
elements: Defendant took, restrained, transported, or confined another person
By force, intimidation, or deception
With intent to hold for ransom, as a hostage, or to commit a felony
enhancements: Victim not voluntarily released unharmed (first degree felony)
notes: First degree felony if victim is not voluntarily released unharmed in a safe place. Reduced to second degree if victim released unharmed.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (occupied/church/business); Fourth degree Felony (unoccupied building); Misdemeanor (personal property <$100)
elements: Defendant maliciously started a fire or caused an explosion
That damaged or destroyed a building, occupied structure, or property of another
enhancements: Person inside at time of fire
notes: New Mexico grades arson by the type of structure: occupied buildings, churches, and businesses are third degree felony. Unoccupied buildings are fourth degree. Small property fires are misdemeanors.

offense_class: Second degree Felony
elements: Defendant performed an act that constituted a substantial step toward commission of murder
With the specific intent to kill another person
enhancements: Use of a firearm (1 year added)
notes: Attempt carries a penalty one degree lower than the completed offense. Attempted first degree murder (capital/first) drops to second degree felony.

statute_title: Aggravated Assault with a Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant committed an assault
With a deadly weapon
A deadly weapon includes any firearm, knife, or instrument that could cause death or great bodily harm
notes: Assault with a deadly weapon is a fourth degree felony. If great bodily harm results, it becomes aggravated battery (third degree felony).

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$250); Misdemeanor ($250–$500); Fourth degree Felony ($500–$2,500); Third degree Felony ($2,500–$20,000); Second degree Felony (>$20,000)
elements: Defendant took anything of value belonging to another
With the intention of permanently depriving the owner
notes: New Mexico grades larceny by value with multiple tiers. Shoplifting has separate provisions under § 30-16-20.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony ($500–$2,500); Third degree Felony ($2,500–$20,000); Second degree Felony (>$20,000)
elements: Defendant committed larceny
Value of property was $500 or more
notes: New Mexico felony larceny begins at $500. The term 'grand theft' is not used in New Mexico statutes but refers to felony-level larceny.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$250); Misdemeanor ($250–$500)
elements: Defendant committed larceny
Value of property was less than $500
notes: Petty larceny covers thefts under $500. Under $250 is a petty misdemeanor. $250–$500 is a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$250); Misdemeanor ($250–$500); Fourth degree Felony ($500–$2,500); Third degree Felony (>$2,500 or third+ offense)
elements: Defendant willfully took possession of merchandise offered for sale by a retail establishment
With the intent to permanently deprive the retailer
Without paying the purchase price
enhancements: Use of anti-theft device removal tools
notes: New Mexico has a specific shoplifting statute. Third offense is a fourth degree felony regardless of value. Civil recovery by merchants also available.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (general); Third degree Felony (dwelling)
elements: Defendant entered a vehicle, watercraft, aircraft, structure, or fenced property
Without authorization
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
enhancements: Burglary of a dwelling (third degree felony)
notes: General burglary is a fourth degree felony. Burglary of a dwelling (residential burglary) is elevated to third degree felony.

offense_class: Third degree Felony
elements: Defendant entered a dwelling house without authorization
With intent to commit a felony or theft therein
notes: Residential burglary is a third degree felony — more serious than non-dwelling burglary (fourth degree).

statute_title: Unlawful Taking of a Motor Vehicle
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (first); Third degree Felony (second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally took a motor vehicle belonging to another
Without the owner's consent
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (third degree felony)
notes: New Mexico has a specific motor vehicle theft statute separate from general larceny. Second or subsequent offense elevates to third degree felony.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant intentionally received, concealed, or disposed of stolen property
Knowing the property was stolen
With intent to deprive the owner
notes: Always a fourth degree felony in New Mexico regardless of the value of the property.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$1,000); Fourth degree Felony (≥$1,000)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged or destroyed property of another
Without the consent of the owner
notes: New Mexico uses 'criminal damage to property.' Damage under $1,000 is a petty misdemeanor. $1,000 or more is a fourth degree felony. Graffiti has specific provisions.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general); Fourth degree Felony (dwelling)
elements: Defendant entered or remained upon posted or fenced property of another
Without permission or lawful authority
After being asked to leave or having notice not to enter
enhancements: Trespass on a dwelling (fourth degree felony under § 30-14-1(D))
notes: General criminal trespass is a misdemeanor. Entering a dwelling without authorization is a fourth degree felony regardless of intent.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$1,000); Fourth degree Felony (≥$1,000)
elements: Defendant intentionally damaged, destroyed, or defaced property of another
Or tampered with property so as to endanger persons or property
notes: Same statute as vandalism. New Mexico calls it 'criminal damage to property.' Includes tampering with utilities and infrastructure.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (first); Misdemeanor (second); Fourth degree Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant committed an assault or battery upon a household member
Household member includes spouse, former spouse, cohabitant, parent of shared child, dating partner
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (fourth degree felony)
Aggravated battery against household member (§ 30-3-16 — third degree felony)
notes: New Mexico has specific domestic violence statutes. Third offense becomes a felony. Batterers' treatment programs commonly ordered.

statute_title: Battery Against a Household Member — First Offense
offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant unlawfully and intentionally touched or applied force
To a household member
In a rude, insolent, or angry manner
First offense
notes: Court typically orders domestic violence offender treatment. Victim eligible for protective order under the Family Violence Protection Act.

statute_title: Abandonment or Abuse of a Child
offense_class: Third degree Felony (endangerment); Second degree Felony (great bodily harm); First degree Felony (death)
penalty_max: 6 years (third degree); 15 years (second degree — great bodily harm); 18 years (first degree — death)
elements: Defendant, being a parent, guardian, or custodian of a child
Intentionally, knowingly, or negligently placed a child in a situation
Which endangered the life or health of the child
enhancements: Great bodily harm resulting (second degree felony)
notes: New Mexico's child abuse statute covers a wide range from endangerment to causing death. Extremely broad — covers placing child in any situation that endangers life or health.

offense_class: Second degree Felony (great bodily harm); First degree Felony (death)
penalty_max: 15 years (second degree — great bodily harm); 18 years (first degree — death)
elements: Defendant intentionally, knowingly, or negligently caused a child
To be tortured, cruelly confined, or cruelly punished
Resulting in great bodily harm or death
notes: Intentional child abuse causing great bodily harm or death carries severe penalties. CYFD involvement accompanies criminal prosecution.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Fourth degree Felony (with prior or involving aggravating conduct)
elements: A valid order of protection was in effect under the Family Violence Protection Act
Defendant had knowledge of the order
Defendant violated a provision of the order
notes: Violation of protection order is a misdemeanor. Repeat violations or violations involving aggravating conduct may be charged as felonies.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Fourth degree Felony (second+ or aggravated)
elements: Defendant knowingly pursued a pattern of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel frightened, intimidated, or harassed
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (fourth degree felony)
Aggravated stalking — in violation of a court order or with credible threat (fourth degree felony under § 30-3A-3.1)
notes: Stalking requires a pattern of conduct (two or more acts). Aggravated stalking is always a fourth degree felony. Includes cyberstalking.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly pursued a pattern of conduct
Directed at a specific person
That was intended to annoy, seriously alarm, or terrorize the person
And that served no lawful purpose
notes: Harassment requires a pattern of conduct (two or more acts). Includes electronic and telephone harassment.

statute_title: Abuse, Neglect, or Exploitation of a Resident
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (general); Third degree Felony (great bodily harm); Second degree Felony (death)
penalty_max: 18 months (fourth degree); 6 years (third degree); 15 years (second degree — death)
elements: Defendant abused, neglected, or exploited a resident or person 65 years or older
Defendant had a duty of care or was in a position of trust
Abuse, neglect, or exploitation was intentional or knowing
notes: New Mexico Adult Protective Services investigates. Covers residents of care facilities and persons 65+. Financial exploitation is separately addressed.

statute_title: Unlawful Carrying of a Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (concealed on licensed premises); Fourth degree Felony (on school premises under § 30-7-2.1)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed loaded firearm or deadly weapon
On licensed liquor premises or school premises
enhancements: Carrying on school premises (fourth degree felony)
Carrying on licensed premises while intoxicated
notes: New Mexico is a shall-issue concealed carry state. Open carry without a permit is legal. Concealed carry without a permit was legalized in 2021 for most purposes. Restrictions remain for schools, bars, and government buildings.

statute_title: Felon in Possession of a Firearm
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant received, transported, or possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony
Possession was knowing
enhancements: Use of firearm in commission of another offense
notes: New Mexico prohibits felon possession of firearms. Some firearm rights may be restored after completion of sentence and waiting period.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (licensed premises); Fourth degree Felony (school premises)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed firearm or deadly weapon
In a prohibited location
Such as school premises, licensed liquor premises, or certain government buildings
notes: New Mexico allows permitless carry in most locations. Schools, bars, and certain government buildings remain prohibited. Carrying on school premises is a fourth degree felony.

statute_title: Negligent Use of a Deadly Weapon / Illegal Discharge of Firearm
offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (negligent use); Fourth degree Felony (if great bodily harm results)
elements: Defendant recklessly or negligently discharged a firearm
In a manner that endangered the safety of another person
notes: Negligent use of a deadly weapon is a petty misdemeanor. If great bodily harm results, it becomes a felony. Local ordinances may impose additional restrictions.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant willfully obtained, recorded, or transferred personal identifying information of another
Without authorization
With intent to defraud the person or to obtain goods, services, or credit
notes: Identity theft is always a fourth degree felony in New Mexico. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$250); Misdemeanor ($250–$500); Fourth degree Felony ($500–$2,500); Third degree Felony ($2,500–$20,000); Second degree Felony (>$20,000)
elements: Defendant, being entrusted with property of another
Fraudulently converted the property to the defendant's own use
Or disposed of the property in a manner inconsistent with the trust
notes: New Mexico has a separate embezzlement statute. Graded by value in the same manner as larceny.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (general); Third degree Felony (government documents, securities)
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud
Falsely made, completed, or altered any writing
So that it purported to be the act of another or was executed at a different time or place
enhancements: Forgery of government documents (third degree felony)
notes: General forgery is a fourth degree felony. Forgery of wills, codicils, contracts, or government instruments is a third degree felony.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (currency/securities)
elements: Defendant falsely made or possessed counterfeit currency or securities
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting of federal currency is typically federally prosecuted. New Mexico's forgery statute covers state-level counterfeiting.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (<$25); Misdemeanor ($25–$500); Fourth degree Felony (>$500)
elements: Defendant issued or delivered a check knowing it would not be paid
Or issued a check with intent to defraud
Check was not honored by the financial institution
notes: Failure to make good within 10 days of notice creates a presumption of intent to defraud.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (general); Third degree Felony (>$2,500)
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false statement or representation
In connection with an insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: New Mexico Insurance Fraud Bureau investigates. Restitution commonly ordered.

statute_title: Fraudulent Use of a Credit Card
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (>$250); Misdemeanor (≤$250)
elements: Defendant used a credit card or account number of another
Without authorization of the cardholder
To obtain goods, services, or anything of value
With intent to defraud
notes: New Mexico has specific credit card fraud statutes. Graded by value obtained.

offense_class: Third degree Felony (<$25,000); Second degree Felony ($25,000–$100,000); First degree Felony (>$100,000)
penalty_max: 6 years (third degree); 15 years (second degree); 18 years (first degree)
elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Knowing the property involved represented proceeds of unlawful activity
With intent to promote unlawful activity or conceal the nature of the property
notes: New Mexico grades money laundering by the amount involved. Fine may be in addition to or instead of imprisonment.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (<$250); Fourth degree Felony ($250–$2,500); Third degree Felony ($2,500–$20,000); Second degree Felony (>$20,000)
penalty_max: Varies by value (same as larceny grading)
elements: Defendant obtained property or services of another by deception or fraud
With intent to deprive the owner
Through false representation, promise, or other deceptive conduct
notes: New Mexico has a general fraud statute. Graded by the value obtained through fraudulent conduct.

offense_class: First degree Felony (great bodily/mental harm, or use of weapon, or multiple perpetrators); Second degree Felony (force/coercion); Third degree Felony (other circumstances); Fourth degree Felony (position of authority)
penalty_max: 18 years (first degree); 15 years (second degree); 6 years (third degree); 18 months (fourth degree)
elements: Defendant caused penetration of another person's genitalia or anus
Or caused another person to make penetration
By force, coercion, threat, or when the victim was incapable of consent
enhancements: Use of a weapon (first degree felony)
Great bodily or mental harm (first degree felony)
Victim under 13 (first degree felony — 25 years to life under § 30-9-11(D)(1))
notes: New Mexico uses 'criminal sexual penetration' rather than rape. Graded in four degrees by circumstances of the offense.

offense_class: Second degree Felony (force/coercion); First degree Felony (aggravated circumstances)
penalty_max: 15 years (second degree); 18 years (first degree); Life (victim under 13)
elements: Defendant caused penetration of another person's genitalia or anus
By the use of force or coercion
Without the consent of the victim
notes: New Mexico does not use the term 'rape.' Criminal sexual penetration by force is the equivalent charge.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (first); Fourth degree Felony (subsequent or to minor under 18)
elements: Defendant knowingly and intentionally exposed primary genital area to public view
Under circumstances likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Exposure to a minor under 18 (fourth degree felony)
Second or subsequent offense (fourth degree felony)
notes: First offense is a misdemeanor. Exposure to a minor under 18 or second offense is a fourth degree felony.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (first); Misdemeanor (second); Fourth degree Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant entered or remained in a house of prostitution with intent to engage in sexual act for payment
Or hired another to engage in sexual activity for compensation
enhancements: Third or subsequent offense (fourth degree felony)
notes: Both patronizing and engaging in prostitution are criminal in New Mexico. Third offense becomes a felony.

offense_class: Second degree Felony (manufacturing/distributing); Fourth degree Felony (possession)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, produced, distributed, or possessed
Any visual or print medium depicting any prohibited sexual act or simulation of such act
Involving a child under 18
notes: Manufacturing and distribution carry significantly higher penalties than possession. Each image/video may constitute a separate count.

statute_title: Failure to Register as Sex Offender
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (first); Third degree Felony (subsequent)
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration
Or provided false information
enhancements: Second or subsequent failure to register (third degree felony)
notes: New Mexico requires sex offender registration for 10 years or 20 years depending on the offense tier. Some offenses require lifetime registration.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (13–16 and defendant 4+ years older); Second degree Felony (under 13)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual penetration with a person under 17
Defendant was 4 or more years older than the victim
Consent is not a defense due to victim's age
enhancements: Victim under 13 (first degree felony — 25 years to life)
notes: New Mexico age of consent is 17 (one of the higher ages in the US). Four-year age difference creates the statutory rape threshold. Victims under 13 face the most severe penalties.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant engaged in violent, abusive, indecent, profane, boisterous, or otherwise disorderly conduct
Under circumstances likely to cause a breach of the peace
notes: Petty misdemeanor — minor offense. Often used as a plea-down from more serious charges.

statute_title: Resisting, Evading, or Obstructing an Officer
offense_class: Misdemeanor (passive resistance); Fourth degree Felony (with force or violence)
elements: Defendant willfully resisted, evaded, or obstructed a peace officer
While the officer was acting in an official capacity
Defendant knew or should have known the person was a peace officer
enhancements: Use of force or violence against the officer (fourth degree felony)
notes: Passive resistance or evasion is a misdemeanor. Use of force or violence elevates to a fourth degree felony.

statute_title: Tampering with Evidence / Obstruction of Justice
offense_class: Third degree Felony (tampering with evidence); Misdemeanor (obstruction)
elements: Defendant destroyed, changed, hid, placed, or fabricated evidence
With intent to prevent investigation or prosecution
Or interfered with law enforcement operations
notes: Tampering with evidence is a third degree felony — very serious in New Mexico. General obstruction is a misdemeanor.

offense_class: Varies (civil vs. criminal)
penalty_max: Varies (up to 6 months for criminal contempt)
elements: Defendant engaged in disorderly conduct in the presence of the court
Or disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or willfully violated a court directive
notes: Direct contempt may be punished summarily. Indirect contempt requires notice and hearing. Court has broad discretion in contempt proceedings.

offense_class: Not a criminal offense (protective custody only)
elements: Person is found in a public place in an intoxicated condition
And is incapacitated or unable to care for self
notes: New Mexico decriminalized public intoxication. Intoxicated persons are placed in protective custody for treatment. Not a criminal offense.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony (if underlying charge is felony); Misdemeanor (if underlying charge is misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or own recognizance
Defendant was required to appear before a court
Defendant willfully failed to appear as required
notes: Penalty depends on seriousness of underlying offense. Court issues bench warrant upon failure to appear. Bond is forfeited.

offense_class: Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly gave false information to a law enforcement officer
About the commission of a crime
With the intent to deceive or mislead
notes: Includes false reports of crimes and false emergency calls.

offense_class: Petty Misdemeanor (general); Misdemeanor (threatening gestures with apparent ability to carry out); Fourth degree Felony (school threats under § 30-20-18)
elements: Defendant communicated a threat to commit a crime against another
With the apparent ability and intention to carry out the threat
Causing the victim reasonable fear
enhancements: Threats against schools (fourth degree felony under § 30-20-18)
notes: General criminal threats are prosecuted as assault. Threats against schools or public buildings have specific felony provisions.

offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant made a false statement under oath
The statement was material to the issue or matter in question
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: Perjury in New Mexico is a fourth degree felony. Requires proof the statement was material. Recantation may be a defense in some circumstances.

statute_title: Bribery of a Public Officer or Public Employee
offense_class: Fourth degree Felony
elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised anything of value
To a public officer or employee
With intent to influence the officer's official act, decision, or vote
notes: Both offering and accepting bribes are criminal offenses. Public officers and employees who accept bribes are also subject to removal from office.

statute_title: Escape from a Community Custody Release Program / Escape from Custody
offense_class: Third degree Felony (from penitentiary); Fourth degree Felony (from other custody)
elements: Defendant was in official custody or detention
Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from lawful custody
Defendant acted intentionally
notes: Escape from the penitentiary is a third degree felony. Escape from other custody (jail, transport) is a fourth degree felony. Sentence is consecutive to underlying sentence.

offense_class: Misdemeanor (general); Fourth degree Felony (extreme cruelty or prior conviction)
elements: Defendant intentionally or negligently mistreated, injured, or killed an animal
Through cruelty, abandonment, or failure to provide proper sustenance
Without lawful justification
enhancements: Extreme cruelty (torture or mutilation — fourth degree felony under § 30-18-1(B))
notes: General animal cruelty is a misdemeanor. Extreme cruelty (torture) is a fourth degree felony. Animal fighting is separately criminalized as a fourth degree felony.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
penalty_max: Original suspended sentence may be imposed
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Court may revoke probation and impose original sentence, modify conditions, or impose graduated sanctions. Burden of proof is preponderance of the evidence.

offense_class: Depends on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: New Mexico Corrections Department Adult Parole Board makes revocation decisions.

offense_class: Same as principal offense
elements: Defendant assisted, aided, abetted, or encouraged another person
In the commission of a crime
With the intent that the crime be committed
notes: An accessory is criminally liable to the same extent as the principal offender. New Mexico treats aiding and abetting as a theory of liability, not a separate offense.

offense_class: One degree lower than the attempted felony
penalty_max: Varies by degree of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by degree of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant performed an act that constituted a substantial step
Toward the commission of a felony
With the specific intent to commit the felony
notes: Attempt to commit a felony is punishable one degree lower than the completed offense. Attempt to commit a misdemeanor is a petty misdemeanor.

offense_class: One degree lower than the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by degree of the target offense
fine_max: Varies by degree of the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons to commit a felony
An overt act was committed by one of the conspirators in furtherance of the conspiracy
Defendant intended that the crime be committed
notes: Conspiracy is graded one degree below the target offense. Requires an overt act. Withdrawal before the overt act is a defense.
